papers.title: Mesoscale molecular architecture of the striatum across cell types and adult aging.
papers.abstract: The human striatum governs diverse motor, cognitive, and affective behaviors yet lacks the obvious cytoarchitectural boundaries defining functional territories elsewhere in the brain. Using Slide-tags single-nucleus spatial transcriptomics, we profiled 1.1 million cells across 19 postmortem donors to uncover the striatum's spatial organization. These data revealed a consistent subdivision of the striatum into six zones, each defined by molecularly distinct populations of spiny projection neurons (SPNs) and featuring spatially coordinated neuron-astrocyte interaction networks. To determine their structural relevance, we generated a companion mouse spatial atlas that identified four homologous zones that aligned with territories defined by brain-wide afferent projections. Finally, imputing zonal identities onto a 131-donor single-nucleus RNA sequencing (snRNA-seq) cohort revealed that dorsal zones exhibit the greatest age-related transcriptional change and that the expression differences defining zonation attenuate with age. This resource establishes a conserved mesoscale spatial framework for the mammalian striatum, linking single-cell molecular identity to structural connectomics and aging.

papers.title: ATF7 coordinates early transcriptional priming to enable direct cardiac reprogramming.
papers.abstract: Direct cardiac reprogramming relies on the canonical transcription factor cocktail MEF2C, GATA4, and TBX5 (MGT), yet successful lineage conversion requires additional non-cocktail regulators that coordinate the chromatin and transcriptional transitions underlying fibroblast-to-cardiomyocyte conversion. Here, we identify Activating Transcription Factor 7 (ATF7) as a critical supporting factor that enables efficient direct cardiac reprogramming. Loss-of-function studies in primary murine cardiac fibroblasts demonstrate that Atf7 knockdown markedly reduces MGT-mediated reprogramming efficiency, with the strongest impairment occurring when Atf7 is depleted during the early priming window of days 0-3. Transcriptomic profiling reveals that Atf7 knockdown disrupts the induction of cardiomyocyte gene programs while restoring expression of fibroblast- and extracellular-matrix-associated pathways, shifting the global expression profile toward a non-reprogrammed state. CUT&RUN mapping across days 0, 3, and 6 of reprogramming shows that ATF7 binds dynamically to lineage-relevant regulatory regions, engaging cardiac loci-including those encoding Gata4 and Tbx5-early in reprogramming, and increasingly occupying fibroblast-associated loci at later stages. Integration of ATF7 binding sites with published single-cell chromatin accessibility data identifies substantial overlap with iCM-enriched regulatory signatures, particularly at day 3, highlighting this stage as a critical node of ATF7 activity. Together, these findings reveal that ATF7 executes a bifunctional regulatory role by simultaneously promoting cardiomyocyte-specific gene activation and repressing fibroblast-associated transcriptional networks. Our study establishes ATF7 as a previously unrecognized regulatory component necessary for efficient MGT-driven cardiac reprogramming and provides a preliminary mechanistic framework for its dual lineage-modulating functions.

papers.title: Subclonal evolution can shape the transition toward a sarcomatoid phenotype in pleural mesothelioma.
papers.abstract: A better understanding of intratumor heterogeneity in pleural mesothelioma (PM) is crucial to implementing precision medicine for this deadly cancer. Using single-cell RNA sequencing approaches on tumor samples and derived primary cell lines, we defined four phenotypic cell types, related to overall survival in larger bulk cohorts: epithelioid, sarcomatoid, intermediate, and nondifferentiated. Some tumor samples showed intratumor phenotypic heterogeneity, associated with subclonal evolution, in which sarcomatoid cells can emerge from parental cells with an intermediate phenotype following the acquisition of copy number variations. Subclones were conserved in cell lines and retained their specific phenotypes, suggesting high phenotypic heritability. Spatial transcriptomics illustrated the link between phenotypic and subclonal evolution, showing that subclonal cells were colocalized and exhibited specific morphologies within the tumor tissue. Our study provides a comprehensive single-cell profiling of PM tumor cells and reveals a link between phenotypic evolution, clonal architecture, and tumor spatial organization.

papers.title: Artificial intelligence and multi-omics integration for cardiac regeneration: from cell fate decoding to clinical translation.
papers.abstract: Heart failure remains among the leading causes of death worldwide, and its burden is increasing as populations age. The adult mammalian heart has almost no capacity to replace cardiomyocytes lost to injury: most cardiomyocytes leave the cell cycle, and the infarcted muscle is replaced by scar, so that function declines progressively. This constraint is not fixed. Neonatal mice regenerate myocardium for a brief window that closes within the first postnatal week, whereas adult zebrafish retain the capacity throughout life; the machinery for regeneration therefore exists, but is held in check. Cell-based therapy was expected to circumvent the problem, yet its clinical benefit has remained modest: transplanted cells survive and engraft poorly, their fate resists precise control, and the host microenvironment actively suppresses regeneration. These shortcomings are symptoms of a single underlying difficulty-scale. The regulatory logic of cardiac regeneration is distributed across transcriptional control, intercellular communication, spatial microenvironments and protein interactions, so that no omics layer examined in isolation, however high its resolution, can recover the integrated picture from high-dimensional, sparse and heterogeneous data. This review proposes an artificial intelligence (AI)-multi-omics integration framework for cardiac regeneration. We survey the methodological progress that becomes available when single-cell transcriptomics, spatial transcriptomics and proteomics are modelled jointly, and examine what these approaches can and cannot establish about cardiac lineage cell fate determination, about regeneration trajectory reconstruction, and about the failing-heart microenvironment. We then consider the translational pathways, and the limits of the evidence for each. The resulting evidence is uneven: the sections on the failing-heart microenvironment rest largely on direct cardiac data, whereas most of the methodological progress has been made outside the heart and transfers only under additional assumptions. One qualification is therefore stated at the outset: evidence for AI in cardiac regeneration is still scarce. The review is positioned as a methodological framework and a forward-looking perspective rather than a synthesis of established conclusions, and the evidence supporting each principal claim is graded, from direct experimental evidence in the heart to methodology.

papers.title: MIF and CXCL8 shape inflammatory myeloid-epithelial crosstalk in cervical squamous cell carcinoma: a machine learning and integrative transcriptomic investigation.
papers.abstract: BackgroundProgression from high-grade squamous intraepithelial lesion (HSIL) to cervical squamous cell carcinoma (SCC) is accompanied by extensive epithelial remodeling and changes in the inflammatory immune microenvironment. However, how stage-specific epithelial states interact with inflammatory myeloid responses, spatial immune organization, and patient prognosis remains unclear. This study investigated these changes and identified inflammation-related molecular features associated with clinical outcome.MethodsSingle-cell RNA sequencing, spatial transcriptomics, bulk transcriptomic and survival cohorts, and drug-response data were integrated. Stage-associated cell states, epithelial trajectories, gene co-expression programs, and predicted cell-cell communication were analyzed across normal cervical tissue, HSIL, and squamous cell carcinoma. Machine-learning survival models were developed in TCGA-CESC and evaluated in GSE39001, GSE52903, and CGCI-HTMCP-CC. Pathway enrichment and immune deconvolution were used to assess biological and immune features associated with the prognostic model. Drug-response prediction, molecular docking, 100-ns molecular dynamics simulations, and immunohistochemistry provided additional computational and tissue-level evaluation.ResultsHSIL was characterized by a proliferative epithelial state, whereas SCC was enriched for an epithelial state associated with keratinization stress, interferon responses, and inferred copy-number abnormalities, accompanied by increased inflammatory myeloid populations. Spatial transcriptomic analysis showed stronger immune and myeloid programs at the invasive front than in the tumor core. Predicted epithelial-myeloid communication in SCC prominently involved MIF-CD74 receptor complexes and CXCL8-CXCR2 signaling. A five-gene prognostic model consisting of MIF, SPP1, CXCL8, CALML5, and CD74 achieved C-indices of 0.748, 0.696, and 0.691 in TCGA-CESC, GSE39001, and GSE52903, respectively. Higher risk scores were associated with hypoxia, glycolysis, TGF-β/EMT signaling, stromal remodeling, and reduced adaptive immune programs. MK-2206 showed favorable predicted interactions with MIF and CXCL8, with greater modeled stability for the CXCL8 complex. Immunohistochemistry confirmed progressively increased CXCL8 and MIF expression from normal cervix to HSIL and SCC.ConclusionProgression from HSIL to SCC was associated with coordinated epithelial remodeling, inflammatory myeloid activation, and spatial reorganization of the immune microenvironment. MIF-CD74 and CXCL8-CXCR2 signaling were implicated in epithelial-myeloid communication, while the five-gene inflammatory model showed reproducible prognostic performance across independent cohorts. These results support further investigation of MIF- and CXCL8-related inflammatory signaling in cervical cancer progression and prognosis.

This unified, cross-species spatial transcriptomics atlas will be a foundational resource for characterizing the molecular and functional organization of the BG and their roles in health and disease.

papers.title: High-Resolution Spatial Transcriptomics Reveals Millimeter-Scale Malignant Territories and Immune Exclusion patterns in Human Salivary Gland Adenoid Cystic Carcinoma
papers.abstract: Background/Objectives Adenoid cystic carcinoma (ACC) of the salivary gland (SGACC) is a rare malignancy with frequent late recurrence and limited response to systemic and immune therapies. Bulk and single-cell sequencing do not preserve tissue architecture, so the spatial organization of its MYB-driven myoepithelial and luminal tumor cells, stroma, and immune cells remains poorly defined. This study aimed to map the SGACC tumor microenvironment at near-cellular resolution. Methods Visium HD based spatial transcriptomics was performed on four SGACC tissue sections from three patients with tubulo-cribriform tumor form in stage III - IV. Bins of 10 x 10 µm were annotated and deconvolved with cell2location using an integrated single-cell reference of 119,189 cells from 20 donors. Pseudobulk differential expression, spatial autocorrelation, potency and spatial trajectory inference, permutation-based territory analysis, Hotspot module detection, and marker-based immune profiling were applied. Results MYB-expressing luminal (LECs-MYB) and myoepithelial (MECs-MYB) epithelial cells occupied 55.7% of bins on average. The MECs-MYB to LECs-MYB ratio increased from the nest interior toward the tumor edge, where cancer-associated fibroblasts rose sharply. Potency and trajectory analyses placed MECs-MYB upstream of LECs-MYB. Malignant states formed territories of up to 38.0 mm² that persisted over 1.5 mm in three sections and contained spatially restricted programs. Hypoxic stressed territories also showed mTORC1, unfolded protein response, and cell-cycle programs. T/NK, myeloid, MHC class I and II, and plasma cell signatures were 1.4-to 5.7-fold higher in stroma than in tumor nests, whereas VTCN1 (B7-H4) was the only B7 family ligand enriched within nests. Conclusions SGACC shows an ordered arrangement of malignant lineages, millimeter-scale malignant territories, MHC class – I and II enriched stroma, and immune-excluded nests enriched for B7-H4. These features provide evidence to be validated in larger cohorts with protein-level and clinical data. Simple Summary Adenoid cystic carcinoma is a rare cancer of the salivary glands that often returns years after treatment and responds poorly to current drugs and immunotherapy. Most earlier studies broke the tumor apart before measuring gene activity, losing the localization of cell in tumor. In this study, we measured gene activity directly on four thin tissue slices from the tumors of three patients at near single-cell detail. The two main types of cancer cells were arranged in an ordered pattern within tumor clusters, and cancer cells of the same type formed large regions several square millimeters in size, each with its own local gene activity. Immune cell signals stayed mostly in the surrounding supportive tissue and rarely reached the tumor clusters, while the tumor cells showed high activity of the gene for B7-H4 that can dampen immune responses. The patient with the longest recorded survival had an altered territory make up from that of other patients that points towards features that studies with larger cohort size can test and develop targeted treatment approaches.

papers.title: velotest: statistical assessment of RNA velocity embeddings reveals quality differences for reliable trajectory visualizations.
papers.abstract: Contemporary single-cell RNA-sequencing studies typically use RNA velocity analyses to investigate cellular dynamics. Commonly, RNA velocities are assessed with two-dimensional projections. Although it is well established that nonlinear embeddings of gene expression data cannot comprehensively preserve the structure of the original high-dimensional data across scales, there is no tool that systematically assesses and quantifies the faithfulness of velocity embeddings. This situation potentially leads to misleading velocity visualizations and putative cell state transitions. To this end, we introduce velotest, a cell-level statistical test that quantifies the faithfulness of a velocity embedding with respect to its high-dimensional counterpart. Applying velotest across multiple datasets and embedding methods, we find strong differences in the embedding qualities between embedding methods, datasets, and regions in individual datasets. velotest thus provides an essential validation step and enables researchers to select a suitable visualization of high-dimensional velocities, ensuring that hypotheses drawn from velocity projections are grounded in accurately represented dynamics.

papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics uncovers pharmacokinetic and tumor-intrinsic determinants of resistance to trastuzumab deruxtecan in breast cancer.
papers.abstract: Trastuzumab deruxtecan (T-DXd) is effective in both HER2-positive and HER2-low metastatic breast cancers, but clinical responses are heterogeneous. Our study identifies spatial features associated with ADC response and resistance in clinical samples and provides a rationale for further investigation of candidate determinants.

papers.title: Intestinal BMP SMADs impart the mid-villus pattern through a transcription factor cascade mechanism.

papers.title: Identification of immune- and cellular senescence-related genes in keloids through integrated transcriptomic and single-cell analysis.
papers.abstract: ObjectiveKeloids are pathological scars resulting from abnormal connective tissue growth in the skin. Protein-protein interaction network analysis was performed to identify hub genes, which were further intersected with single-cell differentially expressed genes to determine key genes. Immune infiltration was assessed using the Cell-type Identification by Estimating Relative Subsets of RNA Transcripts algorithm, and cellular senescence-associated biological pathways were evaluated using single-sample gene set enrichment analysis, gene set enrichment analysis, and gene set variation analysis. Protein-protein interaction network analysis identified 10 hub genes, and integration with single-cell transcriptomic data revealed 5 key genes associated with cellular senescence: cyclin D1, cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1A, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8, galectin 3, and notch receptor 3. Immune infiltration analysis demonstrated significant associations between key genes and immune cell characteristics. Cyclin-dependent kinase inhibitor 1A was correlated with gamma delta T cells and resting dendritic cells, whereas notch receptor 3 was associated with CD8+ T cells and naive CD4+ T cells. Single-cell analysis further characterized the expression patterns of key genes across different cell populations in keloid tissues.ConclusionThis study provides an integrated transcriptomic and single-cell landscape of cellular senescence-related alterations in keloids. The identified key genes are associated with cellular senescence-related transcriptional changes and immune microenvironment characteristics in keloid tissues. Among these genes, C-X-C motif chemokine ligand 8 and notch receptor 3 showed more consistent differential expression patterns at the bulk-transcriptome level, suggesting their relevance in keloid pathogenesis. These findings highlight the potential involvement of cellular senescence-associated programs in the interplay between fibroblast activation and immune alterations in keloids and provide candidate genes for further functional investigation.

papers.title: MuSpec: an unsupervised multi-scale spatial-niche encoder recovers conserved granuloma niches and nominates host-directed repurposing candidates in human pulmonary tuberculosis
papers.abstract: Abstract Background. Tuberculosis (TB) granulomas are spatially organised host–pathogen structures, and the spatial arrangement of immune and stromal cells within the granuloma shapes disease outcome. Spatial transcriptomics can now resolve these structures at single-cell resolution, but most spatial-niche models have been developed and validated on tumour tissue. There is a shortage of unsupervised methods benchmarked on infectious-disease granulomas, and little evidence on how such niche models behave under input noise, missing modalities, and cross-sample transfer — the conditions that decide whether a niche atlas is translational or merely descriptive. Methods. We assembled MuSpec , an unsupervised multi-scale spatial-niche encoder, and applied it to two single-cell-resolution Stereo-seq slides from human TB lung: B1 (pulmonary granuloma; Y40012NC13; 36,382 cells) and P1 (peri-lesional lung; Y40012LA11; 51,834 cells). Each cell was represented as a 39-dimensional input (7-dimensional cell-type composition from cell2location deconvolution against a 146,345-cell peripheral-blood scRNA-seq reference, 30 expression principal components, and 2 spatial coordinates). MuSpec smooths the input at three kNN scales (k = 10/20/30), rasterises each scale onto a ≤ 224² lattice, and passes the three feature maps through four deep-learning modules built on published attention-and-fusion designs — ASFF cross-scale fusion, TripletAttention, ExternalAttention, and a Fourier graph network (FGN) — to produce a 16-dimensional niche embedding; a shared encoder is trained jointly across both slides with an MSE reconstruction loss plus a spatial-smoothing loss, and niches are obtained by KMeans (K = 9). We benchmarked MuSpec against BANKSY at matched numbers of spatial domains, ran a three-seed module ablation and a 34-configuration single-factor hyperparameter sweep, and used the recovered granuloma signature for multi-library signature-reversal drug repurposing (LINCS L1000 chemical perturbations, GEO perturbations, NIBR DRUGseq 2025, and the original CMAP, merged) and AutoDock Vina docking against the host target SP110. Results. MuSpec produced a compact, sub-million-parameter model (782,251 parameters; 93.9% in ASFF) that trains in minutes on a single consumer GPU (≈ 7 GB peak). On every matched-K comparison, MuSpec embeddings separated niches far more sharply than BANKSY (Δsilhouette + 0.31 to + 0.40 on both slides); MuSpec’s own K = 9 silhouette was 0.322 (B1) and 0.285 (P1). Three-seed ablation showed that no module was removable losslessly : removing ExternalAttention lowered niche separation (Δsilhouette − 0.093) but raised robustness and cross-slide transfer (Δ of + 0.137 to + 0.362), identifying a clean separation↔robustness trade-off. For normalisation, a three-seed paired design showed that 7 of 8 robustness metrics changed sign across seeds, so we report no seed-stable difference between global and per-slide normalisation, with only a small stable (+ 0.010 ± 0.003) silhouette advantage to per-slide normalisation on B1. The hyperparameter sweep revealed a monotone separation–robustness frontier with no cliffs, on which the default setting was the robustness optimum (mean noise-robustness ARI 0.758; drop-composition ARI 0.683 on B1 and 0.518 on P1, the highest in the sweep). Joint niche characterisation recovered myeloid/granuloma (SPP1, MMP9, CTSK), airway/club (MUC5B, SCGB1A1, BPIFB1), fibrotic (SFRP2, COL1A1, INHBA) and fibroblast (IL11, TFPI2, PI16) niches, and an SP110–IFN hub analysis. A 324-gene granuloma signature (233 up, 91 down) yielded top signature-reversal hits led by a PPARγ-agonist trio (pioglitazone 90.08, troglitazone, rosiglitazone), and in-silico docking of a focused 6-ligand panel against SP110 gave the strongest affinities for withaferin A (− 7.18 kcal/mol) and nintedanib (− 6.92 kcal/mol). Conclusions. MuSpec provides an unsupervised, reproducible, computationally light route to spatially resolved niche atlases in infectious-disease tissue, and its systematic benchmarking exposes a separation↔robustness trade-off that should be reported rather than hidden. Applied to human TB lung, it recovered biologically coherent, cross-slide-conserved granuloma niches and nominated host-directed repurposing candidates.

papers.title: PIANO enables generative modeling of gene expression and scales multi-omics integration to 100 million cells.
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA technologies enable the routine acquisition of transcriptomic atlases. However, these molecular profiles are influenced by overlapping sources of variation. Since these covariates confound comparisons, data integration is the first step in most analyses. Three challenges remain: correcting strong batch effects, scaling to millions of cells, and modeling how covariates influence gene expression. To address these challenges, we developed PIANO, probabilistic inference autoencoder networks for multi-omics, a deep learning framework whose central feature is a generative model of gene expression data. Additionally, PIANO achieves robust integrations and trains 10× faster than previous methods. PIANO accurately integrates single-cell data across species and across single-cell and spatial transcriptomics modalities. As practical applications, PIANO models spatially resolved gene expression during Alzheimer's disease progression in human brains and integrates over 100 million cancer cells to model drug perturbations. In summary, PIANO's integration and generative modeling capabilities will empower novel insights for a wide range of future studies.

papers.title: Human hair-bearing skin organoids reveal cell type-specific susceptibility and innate immune responses to herpes simplex virus 1.
papers.abstract: Epithelial surfaces are the primary sites of lytic herpes simplex virus 1 (HSV-1) infection following initial exposure or reactivation from latency. While interferon-β reduced viral replication, TNF-α and 4-1BBL did not, suggesting that their primary role is to orchestrate immune cell recruitment and activation. These findings establish human hair-bearing skin organoids as a physiologically relevant model for investigating spatial host-HSV-1 interactions.

papers.title: Single-cell insights into plant responses to biotic and abiotic stresses: cellular heterogeneity and regulatory mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Plants are continuously challenged by biotic and abiotic stresses that compromise growth, productivity, and stress resilience. Although bulk omics approaches have identified numerous stress-responsive pathways, they obscure the cellular heterogeneity and spatial organization that underlie stress perception, signal transmission, and response execution. Single-cell and spatial omics now enable plant stress responses to be resolved at the levels of cell type, cell state, and spatial location. In this review, we synthesize recent applications of single-cell RNA sequencing, single-nucleus RNA sequencing, single-cell chromatin accessibility profiling, spatial transcriptomics, and emerging single-cell proteomics in plant stress biology. We systematically compare biotic and abiotic stresses in terms of spatial response patterns, cellular division of labor, cell-state transitions, and gene regulatory networks. Biotic stress typically generates localized, infection-centered immune landscapes characterized by sentinel-cell activation, vascular defense hubs, and receptor-triggered transcriptional cascades. In contrast, abiotic stress more commonly involves organ-scale homeostatic adjustment, developmental plasticity, and sustained growth-tolerance trade-offs. Despite these distinctions, both stress classes share core regulatory modules, including reactive oxygen species, hormone signaling, transcription factor networks, and vascular long-distance communication. We further discuss technical challenges related to protoplast and nuclei preparation, cell-type annotation, spatial resolution, and multimodal data integration. By linking stress-responsive genes to the specific cell types, states, and spatial domains in which they function, single-cell approaches provide a mechanistic framework for precision engineering and breeding of stress-resilient crops.

papers.title: The evolving immune ecosystem of TKI resistance in EGFR-mutant NSCLC: from treatment-induced remodeling to mechanism-guided therapy.
papers.abstract: Tyrosine kinase inhibitors (TKIs) have transformed the treatment of EGFR-mutant non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), yet acquired resistance remains a major clinical limitation. Finally, we discuss circulating biomarkers, single-cell sequencing, and spatial profiling as tools for longitudinally defining resistant immune states. Viewing TKI resistance as a temporally evolving immune ecosystem provides a framework for linking resistance mechanism, immune phenotype, and treatment selection rather than treating progression as a purely genomic endpoint.

papers.title: Liver immune tolerance and regulated cell death in transplantation and hepatocellular carcinoma: shared mechanisms, divergent outcomes.
papers.abstract: The liver constantly encounters gut-derived antigens, microbial molecules, and food antigens. This environment has shaped a tissue-specific tolerance network centered on tolerogenic antigen presentation, immune-checkpoint activation, regulatory cell expansion, and metabolic suppression. This feature protects the liver during prolonged inflammation and gives it an immunological identity that most solid organs lack. Regulated cell death (RCD) and dead-cell clearance form a critical mechanistic layer within this network. Efficient efferocytosis of apoptotic cells reinforces resolution and tolerance, whereas necroptosis, pyroptosis, and ferroptosis disrupt cell membranes and release danger signals that reshape myeloid activation, T-cell function, and the tumor microenvironment. In liver transplantation, this tolerogenic tendency produces donor-specific hyporesponsiveness, allowing a selected subset of stable recipients to stop immunosuppression while maintaining graft function-a state called operational tolerance. In hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC), tumors exploit the same immunosuppressive axes to block anti-tumor T-cell infiltration and effector function. Anti-PD-L1 therapy combined with anti-angiogenic treatment improves survival, demonstrating that partial disruption of tumor immunosuppression is therapeutically effective. Spatial transcriptomics and single-cell sequencing reveal that SPP1-positive macrophages and cancer-associated fibroblasts form a tumor immune barrier that excludes lymphocytes, showing that hepatic tolerance is organized in space. This duality becomes most dangerous in HCC recurrence after liver transplantation, where immune checkpoint inhibitors boost anti-tumor immunity but also raise the risk of acute rejection, graft failure, and death. Unlike reviews focused on hepatic immune tolerance, regulated cell death, or HCC immunobiology in isolation, this review integrates these processes across the physiological liver, transplantation, HCC, and post-transplant recurrence. We define this coordinated hyporesponsive state as the liver immune tolerance program (ITP), generated by cellular, molecular, spatial, metabolic, and cell-death-related networks. Rather than treating these processes separately, we position RCD and dead-cell clearance as a "death-to-immunity axis," systematically compare ITP remodeling in the physiological liver, transplantation, and HCC, and use post-transplant HCC recurrence as a clinical crossover setting in which graft protection and antitumor immune surveillance become therapeutic considerations. On this basis, we propose precision immune homeostasis: rather than choosing between immunosuppression and immune activation, immune status should be adjusted to an individualized range that protects the graft while preserving anti-tumor immune surveillance.

papers.title: SYNDRI: Context-aware removal of transcript spillover in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Imaging-based spatial transcriptomics (ST) measures gene expression at single-cell resolution, but imperfect segmentation often misassigns transcripts between neighboring cells, a problem known as transcript spillover. papers.abstract: Spatial-omics technologies simultaneously measure feature expression and locations within tissues, providing an unprecedented opportunity to study tissue structures. papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics of cellular heterogeneity in Alzheimer disease.
papers.abstract: Alzheimer disease (AD) is defined neuropathologically by the presence of amyloid plaques and neurofibrillary tangles, yet these canonical lesions alone cannot account for its clinical, regional and cellular heterogeneity. Across individuals, AD heterogeneity is further shaped by sex and ancestry, underscoring the need for broader representation of these factors in single-cell and spatial studies. These advances are also reshaping translational pipelines through multi-omic benchmarking of animal models and single-cell-based drug-repurposing strategies. Thus, single-cell and spatial transcriptomics are redefining our understanding of AD heterogeneity and informing precision approaches to treatment.

papers.title: Premalignant immune remodeling in laryngeal carcinogenesis: a framework to define when immune interception becomes testable.

papers.title: Molecular mechanisms and therapeutic strategies of macrophage-fibroblast crosstalk in gouty arthritis.
papers.abstract: Gouty arthritis is an inflammatory joint disease driven by the deposition of urate crystals, with its pathological core involving innate immune activation and synovial microenvironment remodeling. papers.title: Spatial transcriptomics for gene discovery identifies Slc13a5 as a modulator of bone mechanoadaptation.

papers.title: Senescence-associated stromal remodeling in bone marrow aging and hematologic and bone-metastatic diseases

papers.title: A transcriptomic-driven segmentation and cell simulation framework for high-resolution spatial transcriptomics and cell-cell communication
papers.abstract: High-resolution spatial transcriptomics platforms, such as Visium HD and Atera, enable transcriptome-wide profiling at near-single-cell resolution. papers.title: The predictive dermatome: a technical framework for spatial AI mapping of molecular skin aging.
papers.abstract: Skin aging is spatially heterogeneous. Chronological age and most systemic aging clocks provide useful population-level estimates, but they do not explain why adjacent or anatomically distinct skin regions may show different rates of dermal thinning, matrix remodeling, pigmentation change, vascular fragility, inflammation, or treatment response. We define the Predictive Dermatome as a computationally derived, anatomically localized skin region characterized by a shared or probabilistically related biological aging state and trajectory inferred from integrated molecular, structural, imaging, clinical, and exposomic data. Unlike a conventional neurological dermatome, which denotes a cutaneous territory associated predominantly with sensory innervation from a spinal nerve root, the Predictive Dermatome is not defined by nerve distribution. The proposed framework integrates spatial transcriptomics, spatial proteomics, single-cell or single-nucleus reference maps, optical coherence tomography, confocal or ultrasound imaging, histology when available, tape-strip biomarkers, extracellular matrix and glycation-related measurements, and exposomic data streams. We describe the learning task, input-output structure, spatial graph construction, modality-specific encoders, transformer-based token fusion, training objectives, regularization strategies, and missing-modality handling. Rather than requiring spatial omics or tissue sampling for every clinical patient, the framework uses transcriptomic, proteomic, histologic, and extracellular matrix measurements as discovery and validation layers from which clinically deployable surrogate models could be trained using non-invasive and minimally invasive inputs. We also outline preprocessing steps for high-dimensional spatial transcriptomic data, cross-modal image-omics registration, validation stages, uncertainty estimation, and ethical safeguards including privacy-preserving learning and bias auditing across skin phototypes. The Predictive Dermatome should therefore be viewed as a staged research architecture for precision dermatology, not as a currently validated clinical decision system. Its value lies in defining how molecular geography, imaging, and environmental exposure may eventually converge to support localized risk stratification, longitudinal monitoring, and biologically guided intervention in skin aging and regenerative dermatology.

papers.title: Scar Treatments in Hand Surgery.
papers.abstract: Scar formation after hand surgery poses unique functional and aesthetic challenges because of the hand's complex anatomy, dense sensory innervation, and reliance on supple skin and tendon glide. Hypertrophic scars, keloids, adherent scars, and contractures can cause pain, hypersensitivity, restricted motion, and impaired activities of daily living, yet evidence guiding scar management in hand surgery remains limited and largely extrapolated from burn and general surgical populations. This review synthesizes current evidence on the biology, classification, prevention, and treatment of scars as they pertain to hand surgery. Nonoperative management, including silicone gel sheeting, compression therapy, intralesional corticosteroid injection, laser therapy, and hand therapy, forms the foundation of care. Optimal outcomes depend on a collaborative, individualized approach integrating patient risk stratification, meticulous surgical technique, and close coordination with hand therapy throughout the care continuum.

papers.title: Integrating morphology and spatial omics in gastric cancer: bridging classical mucin phenotypes and molecular stemness.
papers.abstract: Gastric cancer has been described through successive frameworks, each capturing a different dimension of the same heterogeneous tumor. The Lauren, World Health Organization, and Japanese Gastric Cancer Association report histological morphology; mucin phenotyping reports gastric versus intestinal lineage differentiation; and the The Cancer Genome Atlas and Asian Cancer Research Group classifications report molecular state. Bulk profiling averages across tissue compartments, and single-cell approaches, while resolving cellular diversity, discard the coordinates that link molecular state to tissue architecture. papers.title: Disentangling within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Recent advances in imaging-based spatial transcriptomics have enabled high-resolution characterization of gene expression and cellular organization in situ. Resolving within-cell-type heterogeneity is essential for understanding how cellular states relate to tissue function and disease. However, imperfect cell segmentation and RNA spillover can contaminate cell-level expression profiles, obscuring intrinsic expression patterns and generating spurious variation. Existing decontamination methods can struggle to distinguish intrinsic variation from contamination when both are inferred from spatial measurements alone, and may suppress genuine state-associated signals when within-cell-type heterogeneity is not explicitly modeled. Here we present Dancer, a reference-guided probabilistic framework that disentangles within-cell-type heterogeneity from transcript contamination by combining cell-type-specific gene programs learned from single-cell data with explicit modeling of intrinsic expression, neighboring-cell contamination and background RNA. Across multiple human tumor datasets with varying gene compositions and panel sizes, Dancer improves cell-type separation and expression specificity while preserving identity-associated signals, achieving superior overall performance in benchmark comparisons. Inferred gene program activities reveal within-cell-type heterogeneity in the form of distinct cellular states and continuous spatial gradients associated with local tissue environments, while reference-guided panel expansion extends molecular characterization beyond the measured genes. Together, Dancer supports accurate transcript decontamination and more faithful interpretation of cellular heterogeneity within its native tissue context.

papers.title: A noise-corrected metric for evaluating spatial transcriptomics predicted from histology
papers.abstract: Deep learning methods that predict spatial transcriptomics from histology offer scalable molecular profiling of clinical cohorts. However, conventional correlation metrics overstate prediction quality across whole sections by crediting models for recognizing broad tissue regions, and understate fine-scale prediction quality because sampling noise dominates sparse RNA counts. To resolve this, we introduce the reproducible-signal correlation (RSC) metric. RSC randomly splits RNA counts into two halves to separate reproducible signal from sampling noise across spatial scales and within tissue regions or cell classes. Across 12 spot-level and three single-cell methods, RSC revealed that most models capture broad tissue patterns but largely miss differences between neighboring spots or cells, which whole-section correlation overlooks. Within malignant cells, RSC distinguished methods that genuinely capture part of the cell-to-cell heterogeneity from those whose scores across all cells were inflated by cell-type composition. Guided by RSC, we designed a pairwise difference loss between neighboring spots that improved fine-scale predictions on average across 11 models. RSC thus provides a foundation for benchmarking predictions, guiding model design and determining which spatial analyses histology can support.

papers.title: Continuous ex utero development of mouse zygotes to early organogenesis
papers.abstract: In mammals, embryogenesis normally unfolds within the uterus, limiting direct access to the developmental processes that transform a zygote into an embryo with forming organs. Although mouse embryos can be cultured ex utero from early post-implantation stages to mid-gestation, continuous culture from the zygote into organogenesis has not been achieved. Through comparative single-cell transcriptomic and metabolomic analyses, here we discover aberrant BMP signaling and suboptimal metabolic support as barriers to continuous ex utero development. BMP inhibition, together with stage-specific optimization of the culture environment, enables mouse zygotes to progress through peri-implantation development, gastrulation, and into early organogenesis ex utero. Cultured embryos form major embryonic and extraembryonic lineages, establish body axes, and generate multiple organ primordia, while retaining developmental delays and molecular differences from in vivo embryos. By connecting developmental stages that have previously been cultured separately, this study provides an accessible platform for dissecting how early mammalian development progresses into organ formation and a reference for evaluating stem-cell-based embryo models.

papers.title: The cellular neighbourhoods of adult gliomas and their clinical associations
papers.abstract: Glial tumours are the most common primary malignant brain tumours in adults and comprise molecularly and histologically distinct entities with diverse outcomes. Despite this diversity, they arise within a shared anatomical environment, suggesting that common organisational principles may shape tumour heterogeneity. Virtual profiles preserved the direction of all 13 disease-marker differences in measured expression, including tubular injury, maladaptive repair, gluconeogenesis, and fibrosis-associated programs. All 11 measured associations between molecular programs and estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR) were also preserved. Without rat-specific training, a virtual injury score distinguished moderate or severe histopathologic lesions (area under the curve, 0.85) and at least twofold blood urea nitrogen elevation (0.82). papers.title: Single-Cell and Spatial Transcriptomics Identify CDKN2A as a Ferroptosis-Related Regulator of 5-Fluorouracil Resistance in Colorectal Cancer
papers.abstract: Abstract Colorectal cancer (CRC) is a leading cause of cancer-related mortality, and chemotherapy resistance remains a major obstacle to effective treatment. Ferroptosis has emerged as a potential therapeutic vulnerability in drug-resistant tumors, but its role in CRC chemotherapy resistance remains incompletely understood. Transcriptomic analysis identified 28 chemotherapy resistance-related ferroptosis genes. Single-cell analysis showed that malignant epithelial cells had lower Chemotherapy Resistance Ferroptosis Scores (CRFscores) than normal epithelial cells, while CRFscore-low malignant cells exhibited enhanced metabolic activity and tumor-promoting pathway features. CDKN2A knockdown also increased lipid ROS, intracellular labile iron, and malondialdehyde accumulation, while ferrostatin-1 partially reversed these effects. Moreover, CDKN2A depletion reduced PI3K and AKT phosphorylation and decreased SLC7A11 and GPX4 expression. Collectively, our findings identify CDKN2A as a potential regulator linking ferroptosis resistance to 5-FU resistance in CRC and suggest that CDKN2A-associated ferroptosis resistance may represent a therapeutic vulnerability for overcoming chemotherapy resistance.

papers.title: ARC-Impute: robust reference-guided spatial gene imputation through regularised cell-to-spot mapping
papers.abstract: Motivation Reference-guided spatial imputation uses single-cell RNA sequencing references to predict genes that are unmeasured in spatial transcriptomics data. This gives rise to local assignment ambiguity, source-target mismatch and reference-transfer instability. Results We present ARC-Impute, which regularises cell-to-spot mapping through anchor-residual optimisation, target-guided reference curation and routing, and twin-panel consistency. Across 17 human and mouse datasets spanning spot-based and single-cell technologies, ARC-Impute ranked first for held-out Pearson correlation throughout and exceeded the dataset-specific baseline mean by 47.3% on average. It also achieved the strongest spot-level cell-type composition recovery across three pseudospot benchmarks and retained leading accuracy and consistency under reference and training-gene perturbations. Cross-validated predictions revealed systematic differences in gene imputability. Availability and implementation Code and workflows at https://github.com/ethanhaan/arc-impute .

papers.title: Spatial single cell multi-omics identifies divergent melanoma-cell states associated with metastatic outcomes in thin primary melanomas
papers.abstract: Thin melanomas (Breslow thickness ≤1 mm) generally have favorable outcomes, yet some metastasise, highlighting the need for biomarkers of progression. Lineage 1 progressed through an IFN-associated stress intermediate state towards mesenchymal-invasive cells enriched in metastasizing tumors and associated with immune-hot neighborhoods, extracellular-matrix remodeling and angiogenesis, potentially supporting vascular mimicry and metastatic dissemination. Lineage 2 terminated in cohesive nevus-like cells retaining melanocytic features within relatively immune-cold neighborhoods and enriched in non-metastasizing tumors. We confirmed these associations using H&E-inferred spatial transcriptomics in an international multicentric cohort and independent bulk transcriptomic datasets in primary melanomas, linking spatially organized melanoma-cell programs to metastatic outcome and identifying potential biomarkers of progression in thin melanoma. Their distinct microenvironments, protein profiles and transcriptional programs connect cellular heterogeneity to clinical outcome. These associations are supported by independent histological and bulk transcriptomic cohorts of primary melanomas, highlighting the potential of melanoma-cell states for risk stratification. We describe two trajectories that recapitulate the spatial transition from in-situ to invasive melanoma: epithelial-adjacent cells above the dermal–epidermal junction progressed through developmental stress towards a differentiated melanocytic state in the invasive component. From this common trunk, two trajectories extended deeper into the tumor: one towards mesenchymal-invasive cells associated with immune-hot neighborhoods and metastatic outcome; and another one towards nevus-like cells associated with relatively immune-cold neighborhoods and non-metastatic outcome. Proliferation represented an orthogonal program in line with historical dichotomic classification of melanoma cell states (invasive vs proliferative).

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial transcriptomics reveal a cyst-neuron-microglia network underlying brain damage during Toxoplasma gondii infection

papers.title: The STP Open Challenge: A Community Effort to Define and Benchmark Spatial Transcriptome-to-Proteome Prediction
papers.abstract: Abstract While spatial transcriptomics technologies are increasingly accessible, spatial proteomics remains constrained by high costs and limited throughput. Furthermore, poor mRNA-protein correlation, driven by post-transcriptional regulation, necessitates multi-omics integration for complementary biological insights. Current RNA-to-protein prediction models, primarily trained on bulk or single-cell data, often overlook critical spatial context. Consequently, it remains unclear which model architecture, spatial representation, or histopathological features best facilitate spatial protein abundance inference. To address these gaps, we defined the STP (Spatial Transcriptome-to-Proteome) task and launched the STP Open Challenge, a competition for predicting spatial proteomics from spatial transcriptomics of adjacent tissue sections. Utilizing a curated paired spatial dataset and a standardized evaluation framework, the challenge attracted 101 teams and yielded 896 valid submissions. Top-performing methods achieved strong predictive performance while preserving spatial organization. The landscape of submitted models revealed diverse modeling strategies and motivated us to develop a consensus-based ensemble framework that leverages various participant methods to enhance prediction robustness. Extended evaluation on unseen datasets demonstrated that the top-performing models outperformed existing baselines, highlighting the effectiveness of the community effort for this task. By formally defining the STP task and providing a standardized benchmarking platform, this work establishes a foundation for scalable, cost-effective spatial proteomics prediction and future multi-omics integration.

papers.title: Spatial organization of a SPINK1-associated tumor-stromal ecosystem links metabolic remodeling to immune restriction in bladder cancer
papers.abstract: Spatially organized tumor-stromal interactions contribute to metabolic remodeling and immune suppression in bladder cancer (BLCA). These findings identify a spatially organized tumor-stromal niche associated with metabolic cooperation and immune restriction, supporting SPINK1 as a candidate therapeutic target in combination with immunotherapy.

papers.title: RAD: A Read-structure Agnostic Demultiplexer for Single-Cell Long-Read Sequencing and Analysis
papers.abstract: Single-cell long-read sequencing (LRS) techniques enable the analysis of full transcript sequences within a cell. However, LRS introduces computational challenges for parsing information, often necessitating the development of custom workflows to handle complex read layouts, such as split combinatorial barcodes. To address these challenges, we introduce an error-robust, read-structure agnostic demultiplexer (RAD). In RAD, users can easily specify read structure, such as adapter sequence and relative barcode position, and can rapidly extract these elements for each read. RAD implements highly accurate barcode whitelist generation from long-read data alone, without the benefit of short-read support or priors while uniquely avoiding common but previously uncharacterized errors during demultiplexing. RAD's comprehensive barcode error correction protocols allow for more sensitive and precise barcode-read assignments. In synthetic and real-world benchmarks against gold-standard demultiplexers, RAD is faster and achieves better biological discovery capability in downstream gene expression analysis than existing pipelines. We show RAD can be applied to datasets ranging from high-definition long-read spatial transcriptomics to targeted long-read single-cell immune receptor sequencing, making it a powerful and scalable tool for both standard and custom long-read sequencing experiments.

papers.title: NOTCH3 p.R544C Drives Early Neurovascular Unit Dysfunction through Blood-Brain Barrier Failure, Complement Signalling and Metabolic Dysregulation
papers.abstract: Cerebral small vessel disease is a major cause of stroke and vascular cognitive impairment, yet the mechanisms that initiate neurovascular dysfunction before irreversible brain injury remain poorly defined. CADASIL, caused by cysteine-altering NOTCH3 mutations, provides a genetically tractable model to resolve these early events. Here, we investigated the Asian-enriched NOTCH3 p.R544C variant and tested whether early disease emerges through interconnected blood-brain barrier (BBB), inflammatory, and metabolic dysfunction. NOTCH3 p.R544C iPSC-derived endothelial cells showed impaired angiogenesis and migration, reduced barrier resistance, disrupted tight-junction organisation, and altered vascular, adhesion, and extracellular-matrix programmes. In multicellular BBB-like microtissues, these defects propagated across the neurovascular unit, producing disorganised vascular networks, enlarged luminal structures, and increased permeability, establishing BBB failure as an early disease layer. Single-cell transcriptomics revealed coordinated loss of endothelial BBB transport and efflux programmes with astrocytic complement, innate immune, and matrix-remodelling activation. Secretome profiling and patient-plasma measurements converged on complement- and matrix-associated mediators, including C1S and CLU, identifying complement-matrix activation as a second interconnected layer. Importantly, combined cilostazol and isosorbide mononitrate treatment improved barrier function and reduced selected complement- and matrix-associated proteins in mutant microtissues, supporting pharmacological reversibility of components of this early disease programme. Seahorse analysis further demonstrated reduced mitochondrial respiratory capacity associated with NOTCH3 p.R544C. In vivo, three-month-old mutant mice showed altered cerebral pyruvate metabolism and early microvascular abnormalities, whereas six-month-old mice developed more prominent extracellular-matrix, inflammatory, and gliovascular changes, supporting an age-dependent transition from early metabolic dysregulation to broader neurovascular remodelling. Together, these findings define NOTCH3 p.R544C CADASIL as an early multicellular neurovascular disorder organised across three interconnected mechanistic layers: BBB failure, complement-matrix signalling, and metabolic dysregulation, while identifying early BBB-centred dysfunction as a potentially tractable state before advanced cerebrovascular injury develops.

papers.title: Loss of contractile arteriolar smooth muscle cells and their GLP1R expression in human diabetic kidney disease
papers.abstract: Glucagon-like peptide-1 (GLP-1) receptor agonists slow kidney disease progression in type 2 diabetes, and in the human kidney the receptor is localized mainly to arteriolar smooth muscle. papers.title: LUCID: joint cell typing and neighbour-aware decontamination of segmented spatial transcriptomics
papers.abstract: Cell profiles in segmented spatial transcriptomics are contaminated by RNA of neighbouring cells and by segmentation errors that merge two cells. LUCID is a multinomial mixture model that jointly assigns a type to each cell, tests whether its profile mixes two types and estimates the fraction of counts coming from its neighbours. An external reference is adapted to the platform, an identifiability rule protects a cell's own signal and the test is calibrated by parametric bootstrap. LUCID works with or without a reference, runs on CPUs and returns integer counts for all genes. On three public Visium HD datasets (mouse brain, human colorectal cancer, mouse liver) and in simulations built on them, LUCID removed contamination from other cell types as well as a two-step baseline, flagged fewer contaminated cells as mixed, emptied no cell and preserved minority lineages where one cell type dominates.

papers.title: Spatiotemporal profiling reveals emergence of cell type-specific molecular aging and senescence programs in the spinal cord
papers.abstract: The spinal cord is the primary relay center between the periphery and the brain, playing a critical role in sensory, motor and autonomic function. Despite its functional importance, the cellular and molecular changes underlying spinal cord aging and their relationship to cellular senescence – a hallmark associated with aging – remain incompletely understood. Here, we generated a cross-species, multi-omic atlas of spinal cord aging in mice and humans by integrating a combination of liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry, Visium spatial transcriptomics, single-nucleus RNA-sequencing, and multiplexed immunofluorescence imaging. We identified converging age-associated increases in fibrinogen, laminin, and immune activation-associated proteins across the mouse and human spinal cord. Over the mouse lifespan, we further identified distinct spatiotemporal patterns of aging. Downregulated transcriptional programs, including synaptic signaling, mitochondrion organization, and autophagy, were most highly expressed in grey matter regions and in neurons. Upregulated transcriptional programs, including vascular and immune processes, were enriched in white matter regions and in endothelial cells and microglia, respectively. Notably, these increasing spatial modules were also enriched for senescence-associated genes. In the human spinal cord, endothelial cells and microglia were also most enriched for canonical senescence markers CDKN1A and CDKN2A , respectively. Overall, this study defines the shared, spatially-resolved, cell type-specific features associated with aging and senescence in the mouse and human spinal cord.

papers.abstract: Abstract Background Obesity is a global metabolic disorder strongly associated with male infertility, but the spatial and molecular mechanisms underlying testicular dysfunction remain unclear. papers.title: SpaCut: Transcript-Aware Morphology Fusion for Robust Cell Segmentation in Subcellular Spatial Transcriptomics.
papers.abstract: Subcellular Spatial Transcriptomics (SST) offers unprecedented opportunities to decipher tissue architecture at subcellular resolution. Consequently, accurate cell segmentation is a fundamental prerequisite for analyzing SST data, as precise transcript assignment is essential for downstream single-cell interpretation. Existing methods often overlook the spatial organization of transcripts, rely on simplified geometric priors, or struggle to coordinate transcript-derived features with morphology-derived spatial guidance. This limitation restricts their adaptability to irregular cell shapes, often leading to transcript misassignment. To address this, we propose SpaCut, a unified deep learning framework designed to effectively integrate transcriptomic feature learning with dynamic morphological guidance. SpaCut comprises a Gene-Wise Attention (GWA) module and a Nuclei-Guided Attentive Fusion (NGAF) module. GWA encodes the high-dimensional transcript map and aggregates features across multiple depths. NGAF uses the encoded transcript features to modulate distance-based nuclear softmasks and refine nucleus-anchored cell boundaries through progressive training. Extensive evaluations across seven datasets from diverse platforms (including Xenium, CosMx, MERSCOPE, and Stereo-seq) demonstrate that SpaCut significantly outperforms state-of-the-art methods in both segmentation accuracy and consistency with single-cell reference data. The source code is available at https://github.com/wenwenmin/SpaCut.

papers.title: Iterative Geometric Structure Guided Nonnegative Matrix Factorization Scheme for Bulk Tissue RNA-seq Data Deconvolution.
papers.abstract: Complete deconvolution is a class of unsupervised methods that aim to estimate both cell-type proportions and cell-type-specific gene expression profiles (GEPs) from bulk RNA-seq data, without requiring prior reference profiles. Hence, it enables broader applicability to tissues or species for which reference data are limited or unavailable. For many existing methods, nonnegative matrix factorization (NMF) serves as the fundamental computational tool. However, NMF is mathematically ill-posed and a comprehensive understanding of how to overcome the inherent ill-posedness and improve solution accuracy remains lacking. In our previous work, we investigated the necessary requirements for a given bulk RNA-seq dataset to satisfy the solvability conditions in NMF theory. Based on its weak solvability conditions of NMF, a new pipeline of pseudo-bulk tissue data augmented, geometric structure guided NMF model (GSNMF+) has been developed. As a semi-supervised model, it utilizes available single-cell RNA-seq (scRNA-seq) data and has shown obvious improvements in scenarios where the target bulk data contain singular cellular compositions. Nevertheless, when the available scRNA-seq data are not fully consistent with the underlying cell-type-specific GEPs present in the bulk RNA-seq data, it remains a challenge that the deconvolution accuracy will significantly decrease. In this paper, we propose an iterative GSNMF algorithm to address this challenge. First, we propose a new computational algorithm for the GSNMF method (termed as the inner iteration) and provide a theoretical proof of its convergence. We then introduce an iterative process (termed as the outer iteration) to reduce potential discrepancies between available scRNA-seq and the latent cell type specific GEPs in the bulk-tissue data. The proposed methods are evaluated on both synthetic and realistic scRNA-seq data generated bulk-tissue datasets and have shown significant improvements in deconvolution accuracy, particularly in settings where the reference scRNA-seq data are inconsistent.

papers.title: Single-cell and spatial multi-omics for studying cell competition in the tumor microenvironment.
papers.abstract: Cell competition is a conserved fitness-surveillance process, first described in Drosophila epithelia, by which cells compare relative fitness with their neighbors so that less-fit "loser" cells are eliminated, extruded or forced to differentiate while fitter "winner" cells expand. In the tumor microenvironment (TME), this logic appears to be co-opted by transformed clones that eliminate normal epithelium, outcompete neighboring subclones and reshape stromal and immune compartments, making cell competition a potentially underappreciated contributor to cancer clonal evolution, immune escape and therapy resistance. Because competition is defined by a comparison between adjacent cells and by a demonstrated change in the relative representation of one population, it is difficult to resolve with bulk sequencing, which averages across precisely the heterogeneity that defines it. The convergence of single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq), spatial transcriptomics, spatial and single-cell proteomics, artificial intelligence (AI) and network-inference bioinformatics now allows competition-relevant cellular states, interfaces and signaling relationships to be measured at the resolution the problem requires. We emphasize at the outset that these technologies are, in almost all current applications, hypothesis-generating: they identify candidate competitive interfaces and putative winner and loser states from static measurements, and they do not by themselves demonstrate that competition has occurred. This review synthesizes advances across these domains; proposes an explicit three-tier evidence framework separating direct experimental evidence of cell competition from competition-relevant associations and from computational predictions; distinguishes cell competition from related processes such as clonal selection, immune editing and differential proliferation; and defines a putative cell competition network as a falsifiable construct whose edges include ligand-receptor, spatial-adjacency, metabolic and mechanical relations. We further outline a conceptual, context-dependent Cell Competition Score (CCS) as a testable specification rather than a biomarker-ready instrument, and set out the benchmarking, causal-inference and prospective-validation requirements that stand between current capability and any clinical application.

papers.title: Spatial Multi-Omics Integration with Mass Spectrometry Imaging: Decoding Metabolic Landscapes and Disease Mechanisms.
papers.abstract: Spatial multi-omics links molecular measurements to tissue architecture, but integrating spatial transcriptomics with mass spectrometry imaging (MSI) remains challenging because the modalities differ in sampling unit, spatial resolution, data structure, and molecular-identification certainty. Across these applications, spatial colocalization is most informative when annotation confidence is reported and key chemical identities are validated, registration error is quantified, and candidate cell-metabolite relationships are tested by isotope tracing or perturbation. We further discuss molecular ambiguity, resolution-sensitivity-throughput trade-offs, 3-dimensional reconstruction, interlaboratory reproducibility, and requirements for clinical translation. The central conclusion is that spatial multi-omics is best used to formulate anatomically explicit, falsifiable hypotheses rather than to infer causality from aligned maps alone.

papers.title: Nanosecond Pulsed Electric Fields Combined with Triamcinolone Acetonide for Hypertrophic Scar Treatment: In Vitro and In Vivo Evaluation.
papers.abstract: Hypertrophic scar (HS) is a common fibrotic disorder following wound healing for which no universally effective therapy currently exists. papers.title: Wound atlas of Atlantic salmon skin.
papers.abstract: The process of wound healing offers a window into how cells coordinate to maintain tissue integrity, repair damage, and restore tissue function. papers.title: The Role of Tumor-Associated Macrophages in Lung Cancer Progression and Therapy: From Mechanistic Insights to Targeting Strategies.
papers.abstract: Tumor-associated macrophages (TAMs) are among the most abundant immune cells in the lung cancer tumor microenvironment (TME), where their functions vary according to developmental origin, local signals, metabolic conditions, spatial location, and treatment exposure. TAMs can contribute to tumor clearance in some settings but promote immune suppression, tissue repair, and treatment resistance in others. Targeting strategies directed against TAMs, including inhibition of monocyte recruitment, modification of tumor-supportive macrophage states, blockade of phagocytosis checkpoints, and macrophage-directed drug delivery, have demonstrated activity primarily in experimental lung cancer models. However, clinical studies have not yet established the efficacy, selectivity, or safety of these approaches. Major challenges remain, including the high heterogeneity of TAMs, activation of compensatory pathways, systemic toxicity, and the translational gap between preclinical and clinical studies. Future research should focus on validating markers that distinguish disease-associated macrophage states from macrophages required for pulmonary homeostasis and integrating longitudinal tissue, circulating, spatial, and imaging biomarkers. Controlled clinical studies are required to determine whether macrophage-directed interventions can improve existing lung cancer treatments.

papers.abstract: Summary Spatial transcriptomics (ST) has become a central tool in tissue biology, with multiple technologies addressing the issue from a different angle. papers.title: Cancer-associated fibroblasts: origins, functional heterogeneity and therapeutic potential.
papers.abstract: Cancer-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) are integral components of the tumor microenvironment (TME) and are increasingly recognized as critical regulators of nearly every hallmark of cancer. We also explore the compelling evidence for tumor-suppressive CAF functions, which have catalyzed a paradigm shift in therapeutic strategies-moving away from indiscriminate CAF ablation towards nuanced approaches aimed at reprogramming their state. These strategies include modulating key signaling pathways, normalizing the CAF-remodeled ECM, and exploiting unique metabolic vulnerabilities. Finally, we discuss how advances in single-cell and spatial transcriptomics are resolving this complexity, paving the way for the development of precision therapies that can selectively neutralize pro-tumorigenic CAF activities while harnessing their beneficial functions to improve patient outcomes.

papers.title: Auditing Confidence-Calibrated Benchmarking of Single-Cell Perturbation Models
papers.abstract: Single-cell perturbation models are increasingly assessed for both predictive performance and calibrated uncertainty under distribution shift. Most of its headline results measure something other than what their metric names claim. The harness supplied each test cell to the model as input and then scored the model on reproducing that same cell's expression, so an identity predictor returning the input unchanged attains a perturbation-effect correlation of 1.0 on all six splits: any model given the target cell is measured against this echo ceiling rather than against a null. Against a constant train-mean predictor, scVI wins on 99.7% of Norman cells but only 0.2% of Replogle cells. One split held out sequencing batches rather than perturbations; another scores no genuinely novel perturbation after label collapse; unseen perturbations are silently replaced with a negative-control sentinel at inference; and the most convention-sensitive decision-value entry moves 29.2 percentage points under a library-size convention that changes that row's all-gene MSE by 0.01%. Because a validation budget is spent on a ranked shortlist rather than on a marginal interval, we also score each uncertainty signal by the DE-gene error it avoids in the top k: the worst-calibrated method is the best ranker, and a benchmark reporting only coverage orders the two backwards. We document six failure modes, each with its mechanism, the diagnostic that exposes it, and a detection procedure transferable to other harnesses. One result survives, with a boundary condition: split-conformal coverage calibrated on K562 residuals under-covers on RPE1 (0.900 to 0.847), and marginal coverage at the nominal 0.900 is compatible with covering 0.271 to 0.342 of the DE-gene intervals a prioritization decision would rest on. papers.title: Single-Cell Gene Expression Heritability Informed by Genotype x Cell-Context Interactions
papers.abstract: Most signals from genome-wide association studies (GWAS) of complex traits implicate noncoding variants with putative gene regulatory effects. papers.title: Acetate promotes nutritional adaptation in Escherichia coli

papers.title: scINTILLA: Single-Cell Integrated Inference, Labelling, and Landscape Analysis for Assessing the Quality and Hidden Diversity of Cell Annotations
papers.abstract: Single-cell RNA sequencing has made it possible to build atlases of millions of cells, but the cell-type labels in these atlases are rarely checked once they are assigned. When a label covers a transcriptionally heterogeneous population, every analysis that depends on it inherits the problem, and automated label transfer in particular becomes unreliable. We present scINTILLA (Single-Cell Integrated Inference, Labelling, and Landscape Analysis), a framework that scores every label in an annotated dataset from three complementary signals: clustering confusion (neighbours that share a cluster but carry another label), label fragmentation (one label spread over several clusters) and supervised consistency (agreement, confidence and entropy of a classifier ensemble). The three signals are combined into a per-label quality score, scINTILLA-F, which can optionally be rank-fused with the Silhouette width. To test whether the score finds real annotation problems, we injected three kinds of known errors (merged labels, contaminated labels and over-split labels) into five Human Cell Atlas datasets, giving 150 perturbed annotations, and compared scINTILLA with the Silhouette baseline, kNN purity, SCCAF and ROGUE in a pre-registered analysis. The four best of the eleven methods that score every label were all scINTILLA-based. The fusion of scINTILLA-F with Silhouette ranked first (balanced AUROC 0.908; Silhouette 0.896, kNN purity 0.815, SCCAF 0.770) and improved on the Silhouette baseline in every atlas, and adding fragmentation raised the detection of merged labels in every atlas. scINTILLA and the Silhouette baseline were complementary. The Silhouette baseline was better at finding merges, whereas scINTILLA was better at finding over-split labels. Applied to the real atlases, scINTILLA flagged the ``Unknown'' and monocyte-derived macrophage labels of the lung atlas and the ``stem cell'' label of the endoderm organoid atlas. Re-analysis of these populations resolved disease-associated monocyte and macrophage states and a set of progenitor, stromal and differentiated identities with distinct tissue and protocol origins. Finally, we tested the score on merges that arise naturally, in a leukaemia atlas of 183 patients whose blast populations we had annotated. Label fragmentation revealed the diversity of the blasts hidden under a patient label: in acute myeloid leukaemia it was higher in patients whose blasts formed several populations. In each of these cases scINTILLA pointed to the labels that needed a closer look, and the interpretation remained with the expert. It is therefore advisory: it ranks labels for expert review and shows which signal flagged each one.

papers.title: CellBench: task-dependent performance and generalization limits of single-cell foundation models
papers.abstract: Single-cell foundation models (scFMs) are increasingly used for transcriptomic analysis, yet it remains unclear what biological information their embeddings preserve and when they outperform dataset-fitted methods. papers.title: Spatial proteomics identifies a myeloid-dominated, compartmentalized microenvironment and a proliferation-associated prognostic signature in clear cell sarcoma
papers.abstract: Clear cell sarcoma (CCS) is a rare soft-tissue sarcoma with poor prognosis and limited therapeutic options. Finally, we identified c-MET and B7-H3 as candidate antibody-drug conjugate targets without significant regional or primary-metastasis differences in expression. Together, this work illuminates the spatial proteomic landscape of CCS and highlights candidate markers for patient stratification and potential therapeutic targets.

papers.title: Scalable cell-state-resolved TWAS identified dynamic autoimmune disease genes along functional programs
papers.abstract: Transcriptome-wide association studies (TWAS) are widely used to prioritize genes for complex diseases. TWAS typically trains models on expression quantitative disease locus (eQTL) reference data to predict gene expression from genotype, then tests for association between the predicted expression and disease. Here we propose Fast-TWiST, an accelerated and scalable version of TWiST that can analyze hundreds of thousands to millions of cells. Fast-TWiST computes donor-level summary statistics that retain all the information needed to fit the cell-level model, so numerical optimization runs over donors rather than individual cells. In simulations and real-data evaluations, Fast-TWiST was more than 10 times faster than TWiST while matching its statistical performance. papers.title: MetaEntropy: quantifying protein variability in complex viral mixtures via entropy
papers.abstract: High-density sequence data has become commonplace in the study of complex viral mixtures from wastewater. Established algorithms are available for lineage deconvolution and labelling of clinically-elusive mutations. MetaEntropy integrates utility functions for visualizing genome-wide and protein-specific variability, extracting nucleotide and amino acid mutation profiles, and identifying entropy hotspots. However, it does not analyze population structure or quasispecies, for which several tools are available. Calculated entropy values are normalized to a 0-1 scale, enabling direct comparisons of protein diversity across loci and sample strata. As proofs of concept, we employ MetaEntropy to detect well-known SARS-CoV-2 functional changes from wastewater data, and to explore tissue-specific heterogeneity in systemic infections. papers.title: All the diversity we cannot see: Using single-cell population genetics to reveal the reproductive mode of the snow alga Chlainomonas sp. (Chlorophyta)
papers.abstract: Many organisms responsible for globally important processes, from carbon cycling to human disease, are microscopic eukaryotes. We found high selfing rates, but selfing and clonality are often indistinguishable without understanding an organisms's natural history. Chlainomonas sp. has a haploid-diploid life cycle as hypothesized, engaging in both clonal and sexual reproduction, likely selfing. papers.title: Loss of SRF-driven contractility, not lymphatic smooth muscle cell loss, is the primary driver of age-associated collecting vessel decline
papers.abstract: The lymphatic vasculature returns interstitial fluid to the blood circulation, a function that depends on rhythmic contraction of the smooth muscle cells (SMCs) surrounding collecting vessels. papers.title: Inactive X chromosome DNA methylation erosion with age in human dermal fibroblasts
papers.abstract: X chromosome inactivation is an epigenetic process that establishes dosage compensation between the sexes through the monoallelic silencing of one X chromosome in karyotypically normal females. The allele that becomes inactivated is determined randomly during early development, resulting in females being mosaic with respect to whether the maternal or paternal allele is inactivated. This mosaicism makes it technically challenging to separate the active and inactive chromosomes in bulk populations, and consequently it has been historically difficult to study X chromosome inactivation in human cells. Notably, we observe substantial loss of DNA methylation across multiple CGIs on the inactive X chromosome in an age dependent manner. We also observe this DNA methylation erosion in bulk samples by quantifying CGI methylation levels across individual sequencing reads. The genes that show age-related erosion of CGI methylation are associated with increased total transcription suggesting this methylation erosion generates a transcriptional permissive state. Overall, our study provides evidence of erosion of X chromosome inactivation with age in cell lines derived from primary human samples and implicates a role for loss of DNA methylation in the increased dosage of X chromosome linked genes in females with age. These findings shed new light on the epigenetic instability of the inactive X chromosome during human ageing and may be linked to age-related cellular dysfunction in females.
